topic: Sharp fixed-areal boundary-effect sets by clipping-aware partial transport. For a polygonal geographic RD observed through finitely many known areal score laws and bounded cell outcomes, characterize the exact mean-information set of the weighted boundary-average effect over [0,1]-valued Lipschitz potential-outcome surfaces. Prove attained causal endpoints, the clipping-aware partial-transport value dual without a multiplier-sum restriction, finite multiplier attainment on the relative interior and the zero-mean boundary obstruction. Derive the complete rectangle, nonuniform-density, and weighted-triangle formulas; give universally convergent atomic outer programs, relative-interior exact-moment piecewise-affine inner programs with a posteriori gaps, and simultaneous finite-sample whole-set coverage by cell-mean confidence-box inversion. Consumer: Dell's bounded child-stunting mita-boundary outcome receives a resolution-honest sign certificate. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Derived the exact unmatched-mass transport identity, sharp Bernoulli endpoint lifting, all three planar formulas, and a relative-hull moment correction with loss epsilon_h(1+sqrt(J)/r); smoothing/interpolation yields epsilon_h=O(sqrt(h)) and an outer error bound 2Mh(1+sqrt(J)/r). Exact arithmetic certified the triangle witness, forty rectangle LPs and three planar SOCPs passed, and 35 support-versus-flow checks agreed to 8.9e-16. Boundary finite-multiplier nonattainment, radial exposed faces, incompatible means, full-law failure, and current Qiu-Stoye/Piccoli-Rossi collisions were checked and scoped out. The revised scope preserves only the mean-information target and relative-interior certification. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Establish a terminating verified primal-reconstruction and dual-enclosure routine that preserves exact continuous cell moments and returns arbitrarily small outward-certified endpoint gaps for every fixed relative-interior mean. EARLY KILL TEST: On a rational two-cell planar strict-interior instance, produce an exact continuous piecewise-affine witness and outward dual enclosure with shrinking verified gap; floating residuals or nonconvergent gaps kill the computational claim. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_areal_rd_transport_modulus.md.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp identified interval for a weighted boundary-average treatment effect when only finitely many exact areal means and score laws are observed and each potential-outcome surface is [0,1]-valued and Lipschitz?

source_refs.claim: They formulate tight multivariate Lipschitz bounds, then use a one-coordinate relaxation and drop the bounded-effect constraint for tractability; they explicitly identify development of the tight bounds as an open extension.
source_refs.author: Chen Qiu and Jörg Stoye
source_refs.venue: Advances in Economics and Econometrics, Thirteenth World Congress, Cambridge University Press (forthcoming)

source_refs.claim: The paper defines boundary-aggregated causal effects and develops pre- and post-aggregation estimators from unit-level observations, but does not characterize the identified set from fixed areal means.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocío Titiunik, and Ruiqi Rae Yu

source_refs.claim: Their generalized W1 distance supplies a bounded-Lipschitz dual for unequal-mass measures, but it does not incorporate exact areal side moments or the asymmetric clipping costs generated by bounded potential-outcome surfaces.
source_refs.author: Benedetto Piccoli and Francesco Rossi
source_refs.venue: Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis

open_problems.why_unsolved: Boundary-discontinuity methods identify or estimate effects from observations approaching the boundary, whereas fixed areal data reveal only integrals of two latent potential-outcome surfaces. The [0,1] range clips their Lipschitz envelopes and converts unmatched signed mass into a partial-transport problem; exact cell means add affine constraints absent from the standard flat-metric dual. Qiu and Stoye obtain a tractable expression only after relaxing the full multivariate constraint, while the aggregation literature continues to use unit-level boundary observations.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving attained lower and upper causal endpoints, an equivalent clipping-aware partial-transport primal and multiplier dual without a multiplier-sum restriction, and closed-form endpoint formulas for specified polygon-density-weight families.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from a boundary policy decision to smoothness-based partial identification and states candidly where its tractable relaxation departs from the tight problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A policy decision depends on effects beyond an observed boundary -> smoothness converts limited boundary information into a feasible effect interval -> tractable projection bounds relax the multivariate bounded-surface problem -> recover the exact mean-information set from areal data.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the deletion-plus-transport primal and bounded-Lipschitz dual proof, replacing symmetric deletion penalties by pointwise clipping costs and adjoining exact-moment multipliers.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both optimize Lipschitz functionals against unequal-mass signed measures; the desired endpoint is a constrained, spatially weighted flat-metric analogue.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the generalized-moment representation of transport plans and convergent moment/SOS truncations to obtain value-level outer approximations on polygonal semialgebraic supports.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoint is an optimal-transport value with finitely many side moments, matching their measure-optimization representation.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over their location-based boundary parameterization and uniform boundary empirical-process argument, replacing a point-valued boundary-effect curve by estimated support functions of the sharp interval.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest boundary-aware large-sample theory while respecting the polygonal geometry that scalar distance methods can miss.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct a terminating verified algorithm that, for every rational polygonal strict-relative-interior areal mean vector and tolerance ε>0, returns an exactly moment-feasible continuous piecewise-affine primal surface and a rigorous dual enclosure whose endpoint gap is at most ε?

source_refs.claim: Their moment-SOS hierarchy proves asymptotic convergence of optimal-transport values and approximates linear quantities and support locations, but does not give exact continuous primal reconstruction with a finite stopping certificate.
source_refs.author: Olga Mula and Anthony Nouy

source_refs.claim: Their effective atomic recovery from moment relaxations depends on flat truncation, tied to zero-dimensional minimizing support or additional regularity rather than continua of Lipschitz optimizers.
source_refs.author: Lorenzo Baldi and Bernard Mourrain

open_problems.why_unsolved: Value convergence of a discretized or moment-SOS relaxation is not a verified primal certificate: a floating atomic optimizer generally misses the prescribed continuous cell moments, while flat-extension recovery can fail for positive-dimensional optimizer support. Correcting the moments may violate clipping or the global Lipschitz inequalities, and checking a dual only on a grid does not certify its behavior between grid points. Existing moment-transport work therefore leaves open the first proof step needed here: converting relative-interior slack into exact continuous feasibility and a finite two-sided stopping certificate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit rational-arithmetic refinement algorithm with a proved stopping rule that preserves every continuous cell moment exactly, constructs a feasible [0,1]-valued Lipschitz piecewise-affine witness, and outputs outward-certified rational endpoint bounds separated by at most ε.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames computation as a generalized moment problem and clearly distinguishes asymptotic value approximation from recovery of an optimizing transport object.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Continuous transport is infinite-dimensional -> moment truncations yield finite semidefinite relaxations -> asymptotic value convergence does not itself produce an exactly feasible optimizer -> add verified reconstruction and a terminating outward gap.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt their generalized-moment encoding and monotone relaxation hierarchy to generate rigorous value-side outer bounds for the clipping-aware partial-transport endpoint.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required dual enclosure is a certified hierarchy for a transport problem with finitely many prescribed moments.

method_exemplars.technique: Use flat-truncation tests and representing-measure extraction when available, then replace that proof step by a relative-interior moment-correction construction when the optimizer has positive-dimensional support.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It isolates exactly when truncated moments can be converted into an exact atomic measure and therefore exposes the missing reconstruction step for continuous Lipschitz extremizers.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine effective positivity certificates and quantitative control of truncated pseudo-moments with mesh interpolation bounds to derive computable outward dual errors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A terminating certificate needs quantitative separation between pseudo-moment relaxations and genuine feasible measures, not merely qualitative convergence.

open_problems.open_problem: Can cell-mean confidence-box inversion provide simultaneous finite-sample coverage of the entire sharp areal boundary-effect interval under known score laws, while remaining Hausdorff-consistent at nonsmooth endpoint regimes?

source_refs.claim: Their application assumes the score distribution and normal variance are known and uses an asymptotic Gaussian approximation rather than finite-sample whole-set coverage.
source_refs.author: Chen Qiu and Jörg Stoye
source_refs.venue: Advances in Economics and Econometrics, Thirteenth World Congress, Cambridge University Press (forthcoming)

source_refs.claim: They establish pointwise and uniform inference for local-polynomial boundary-effect estimates from individual bivariate scores, not whole-set inference obtained by inverting aggregate moment uncertainty.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Rocío Titiunik, and Ruiqi Rae Yu
source_refs.venue: Working paper; Journal of the American Statistical Association revise-and-resubmit

source_refs.claim: They derive asymptotic confidence regions for identified sets by criterion inversion, but not finite-sample confidence-box propagation through an infinite-dimensional Lipschitz transport endpoint map.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, and Elie Tamer

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two endpoints are support values of a constrained infinite-dimensional feasible set and can be nondifferentiable as cell means approach exposed faces. Pointwise Gaussian inference for a boundary effect does not automatically cover both endpoints and the full interval simultaneously. Finite-sample inversion of joint bounded-mean confidence boxes has the correct monotonicity in principle, but still requires a proof of set inclusion, measurability, and shrinking Hausdorff error that accommodates multiplier nonattainment on boundary mean vectors.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A confidence-box inversion procedure with a theorem guaranteeing at least 1−α finite-sample coverage of the whole sharp interval and Hausdorff consistency under explicit cell-size, relative-interior, and geometric conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its application cleanly separates identification uncertainty from sampling uncertainty and identifies the known-distribution and Gaussian steps on which its policy calculation relies.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A boundary identified set determines whether a policy effect has a certified sign -> cell outcomes are observed with sampling error -> pointwise Gaussian inference does not cover the complete feasible interval -> invert simultaneous cell-mean boxes to obtain honest whole-set coverage.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt criterion-set inversion and its Hausdorff analysis to the support-function endpoint program, using a joint cell-mean confidence box instead of a scalar sample criterion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The inferential target is the entire set of feasible causal effects rather than a single unknown point inside it.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over bias-aware honest critical-value reasoning for linear functionals over smoothness classes, replacing regression-bias maximization by exact optimization over the Lipschitz areal-information class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems require uniform coverage over a nonparametric Lipschitz class while retaining informative finite-sample conclusions.

method_exemplars.technique: Use their bivariate-score boundary parameterization and uniform inference as the unit-level benchmark, then propagate simultaneous moment uncertainty through the partial-identification endpoint map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest inference theory that treats polygonal boundary geometry as a first-class feature.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the exact, generally non-nested identified set for an areal boundary-average effect when [0,1]-valued potential-outcome surfaces satisfy both Lipschitz smoothness and comonotonicity, and how can its endpoints be estimated with valid limit theory?

source_refs.claim: They explicitly propose combining comonotonicity with smoothness, note that it induces non-nested partial identification, and state that even asymptotic normality is not obvious.
source_refs.author: Chen Qiu and Jörg Stoye
source_refs.venue: Advances in Economics and Econometrics, Thirteenth World Congress, Cambridge University Press (forthcoming)

source_refs.claim: They identify extrapolated weighted RD effects under comonotonic conditional mean potential outcomes and propose local-linear estimation, but do not derive the sharp set when comonotonicity is combined with Lipschitz restrictions and only areal moments are observed.
source_refs.author: Ben Deaner and Soonwoo Kwon

open_problems.why_unsolved: Comonotonicity couples the rankings of the two latent response surfaces and is neither a separate convex restriction on each surface nor equivalent to a bound on their difference. With only cell integrals, the admissible within-cell rankings remain latent; intersecting that ordering restriction with global Lipschitz and clipping constraints destroys the simple convex partial-transport representation and can make identified sets non-nested. Deaner and Kwon use richer local variation for their identification argument, while Qiu and Stoye explicitly flag the combined sharp-bounds and limit-law problem as unresolved.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp characterization of the feasible boundary-effect set under joint comonotonicity, Lipschitz, clipping, and areal-moment constraints, together with an endpoint estimator and a uniform or directional-delta limit theorem yielding valid confidence sets.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames comonotonicity as an economically interpretable alternative to constant effects for extrapolation away from an RD margin.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: RD identifies effects only at a treatment margin -> policy questions require extrapolation away from that margin -> comonotone response rankings provide structured extrapolation without constant effects -> determine the sharp implications when only areal means and Lipschitz smoothness are available.

method_exemplars.technique: Start from their Lipschitz projection-bound formulation, then replace the one-coordinate adversary by a jointly rank-constrained pair of bounded potential-outcome surfaces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the boundary-policy estimand and smoothness-based feasible interval into which comonotonicity must be integrated.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt their comonotone ranking argument and local-linear construction, replacing point extrapolation by optimization over latent within-cell orderings and deriving the directional behavior of the resulting endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the directly matched RD method built around comonotonic conditional mean potential outcomes.

method_exemplars.technique: Use their connection between partial-identification geometry and constraint qualifications to characterize where endpoint sensitivity and standard limit theory hold or fail.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The non-nested rank-constrained set creates the boundary and constraint-qualification failures that a valid endpoint theorem must control.

literature_map:
Dell (2010, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA8121) is the empirical anchor: the mita-boundary RD reports an increase in child stunting, a naturally bounded outcome.
Keele and Titiunik (2015, Political Analysis, doi:10.1093/pan/mpu014) formalize geographic RD as a two-score design and emphasize geographic identification and validation issues.
Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu (2025, Causal Treatment Effect Aggregation) distinguish pre- and post-aggregation boundary effects, but retain unit-level observables rather than fixed areal means.
Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu (2025, arXiv:2505.05670) give location-based pointwise and uniform boundary inference and show why respecting bivariate geometry matters.
Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu (2026, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2510.26051) show that distance-based methods incur geometry-dependent misspecification bias near irregular boundaries.
Qiu and Stoye (2026, arXiv:2601.17648) are the closest collision: they formulate tight multivariate Lipschitz bounds but compute a one-coordinate relaxation, drop clipping for simplicity, assume the score law and variance known, and explicitly request tighter bounds.
Deaner and Kwon (2025, arXiv:2507.00289) use comonotonic conditional mean potential outcomes for RD extrapolation; Qiu and Stoye note that combining this restriction with smoothness yields non-nested partial identification and non-obvious asymptotics.
Piccoli and Rossi (2016, ARMA, doi:10.1007/s00205-016-1026-7; arXiv:1304.7014) identify unequal-mass generalized W1 with a bounded-Lipschitz metric, supplying the closest transport duality but no exact areal side moments.
Liero, Mielke, and Savaré (2018, Inventiones, doi:10.1007/s00222-017-0759-8) place unbalanced transport in a broader entropy-transport framework; its divergences do not directly encode outcome clipping and exact cell means.
Mula and Nouy (2024, Numerische Mathematik, doi:10.1007/s00211-024-01422-x; arXiv:2211.10742) prove convergent moment-SOS transport hierarchies and approximate recovery, but not terminating exact-moment continuous primal certificates.
Baldi and Mourrain (2025, Journal of Symbolic Computation, doi:10.1016/j.jsc.2024.102403; arXiv:2012.14652) connect exact moment recovery to flat truncation and support regularity, exposing the obstacle for continua of Lipschitz optimizers.
Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari (2011, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA8680) characterize sharp convex moment-prediction sets through support functions, a natural language for areal mean-information sets.
Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2022, Econometric Theory, doi:10.1017/S0266466621000207) connect partial-ID geometry to constraint qualifications, directly relevant to relative-interior multiplier attainment and boundary failure.
Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007, Econometrica, doi:10.1111/j.1468-0262.2007.00794.x) develop criterion-inversion inference for identified sets; Imbens and Manski (2004, Econometrica, doi:10.1111/j.1468-0262.2004.00555.x) distinguish covering the whole interval from covering a true point.
Armstrong and Kolesár (2020, Quantitative Economics, doi:10.3982/QE1199; arXiv:1606.01200), Kolesár and Rothe (2018, AER, doi:10.1257/aer.20160945), and Ishihara, Sawada, and Yata (2025, arXiv:2509.18857) supply nearby honest or minimax inference machinery for smooth RD response functions.
